CrossSeq2.notes: Written from the maker's source at commit 5ebe71e, the last of the three commits whose plugin.json carries 2.1.6.0; the installed manifest's authorUrl, 'https://linktr.ee/michelezac', matches 9d79d54 and 5ebe71e rather than the earlier a903f08, and no DSP file differs between any of those three or the repository head. The DSP is written in Vult and compiled to C++; CrossSeq2.vult is the readable form and CrossSeq2.cpp the generated one. The panel prints only the row labels rt, am, sh, ph and pw, with the left column belonging to LFO 1 and the right to LFO 2; the individual knobs carry no lettering. The freq input is the only CV input with no attenuverter, and it is the only one added at full voltage rather than divided by ten. Nothing in the module clamps the master frequency, so a negative freq input drives the phase increment negative, and the phase wrap in lfo_interp only wraps downward from above 2.0.

CrossSeq3.notes: Written from the maker's source at commit 5ebe71e, the last commit carrying 2.1.6.0. Two differences from XSeq2 that the README does not mention and that are not visible on the panel. First, the phase knobs: CrossSeq2Module.cpp:101 passes the phase knob multiplied by two into a phase that runs 0 to 2, so on XSeq2 the knob covers a whole cycle, while CrossSeq3Module.cpp:140 passes it unmultiplied, so on XSeq3 the same knob covers half a cycle. Second, the shape attenuverters are configured -3 to 3 here and -1 to 1 on XSeq2. The 1x2x3 output is not a trigger like the other three: cross_detect3 in CrossSeq3.vult returns 1 for as long as the three absolute differences sum to less than 0.1, so it is a gate whose length follows how slowly the LFOs pass each other, and it has no minimum length. The d123 output is (lfo1 - lfo2) - lfo3, which is asymmetric and is not what the 1x2x3 output tests. Index order is not panel order in the output row: the diff jacks are indices 7 to 10 and sit above the trigger and LFO jacks, which are indices 0 to 6.

Carries 10V for the length set by this section's gate knob after each trigger, and 0V the rest of the time
Note — neither output is given a name in the code, so hovering either one shows no tooltip at all
Note — the two sections share nothing: each has its own trigger, its own length knob and its own gate, and neither affects the other

TrigGate.notes: Written from the maker's source at commit 5ebe71e, the last commit carrying 2.1.6.0. The constructor calls configInput for both trigger jacks and configOutput for neither, so the two gate outputs have no tooltip; the census records both output names as blank. The gate length is a plain accumulation of sampleTime, so the knob's 0 to 1 is 0 to 1 second at any sample rate. With the knob at exactly zero, trig2gate in TrigGate.vult reaches its open state with dur at 0 and len at 0: neither 'dur < len' nor 'dur > len' is true, so the state is never cleared and the gate stays high until the patch is reloaded. Both length knobs are read once every four samples; the trigger inputs are read every sample. The panel prints the module as T2G and labels the jacks trig and gate.

lines: Passes a trigger through to one output or the other according to two tests made on two signals, which are usually LFOs
Chooses what is tested on the lfo1 input: dir tests which way that signal moved between this sample and the last, sign tests whether it is above or below 0V
Chooses what is tested on the lfo2 input: dir tests which way that signal moved between this sample and the last, sign tests whether it is above or below 0V
Sets what the lfo1 test has to find for that side to pass: plus for rising or positive, minus for falling or negative, zero for no change at all or exactly 0V
Sets what the lfo2 test has to find for that side to pass: plus for rising or positive, minus for falling or negative, zero for no change at all or exactly 0V
Chooses whether both sides have to pass before a trigger reaches the trig output, or only one of them
The trigger to be passed or blocked; whatever voltage is here appears unchanged at whichever of the two outputs the tests send it to
The first of the two signals tested
The second of the two signals tested
Carries the voltage at the trig input while the tests pass, and 0V while they do not
Carries the voltage at the trig input while the tests do not pass, and 0V while they do, so between them the two outputs let every trigger through somewhere
Note — with dir selected, the zero setting is almost never matched, because a moving signal changes by some amount at every sample; it matches an unpatched jack, which never changes at all
Note — the two switches and the two small knobs are read once every four samples, while the trigger and the two signals are read every sample

TrigLogic.notes: Written from the maker's source at commit 5ebe71e, the last commit carrying 2.1.6.0. Index order is not panel order on either row: the inputs read lfo1 (index 1), trig (index 0), lfo2 (index 2) from left to right, and the outputs read invert (index 1) then trig (index 0). The panel letters the two small knobs '- / 0 / +' while the maker's tooltip calls them 'up/zero/down'; the panel is what the reader is looking at, so the line uses plus, minus and zero. The lfo2 input's tooltip is spelt 'lof2' in the source and so reads that way in the rack. Neither output has a family-defining voltage of its own: they pass the trig input's voltage through unchanged, divided by ten on the way in and multiplied by ten on the way out. The and/or switch is configured with 'or' at 0 and 'and' at 1 and defaults to 'or', although the Vult code's own default sets it the other way; the module writes the parameter into the processor every four samples, so the parameter wins from the first block.
